topic: Exact attrition-robust randomization inference for an explicitly weighted fixed-count assignment support: under a sharp additive null, arbitrary treatment-indexed observation indicators, and Wilcoxon treated-rank sums with midranks, characterize the supremum exact upper-tail p-value over all legal missing-outcome completions by a complete weak-order chamber complex. Prove unconditional finite-sample validity, an explicit O((2n+1)^k n|Omega| poly(bits)) algorithm with a linear one-missing sweep, O(n^2) additive-effect inversion, and NP-completeness of EXPLICIT-MAX-TAIL for variable k by an explicit rational weighted-support CLIQUE reduction. Include the constrained six-unit non-extreme-completion witness, the equality-face witness, and a conditional saved-support corollary for a prospective cvcrand rank option on prespecified cluster endpoints; do not claim hardness for uniform balance-generated supports or unchanged cptest applicability. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Two independent presolves derived weak-order attainment and oracle-tail domination for arbitrary treatment-indexed masks; reconstructed the fixed-k and k=1 algorithms and finite effect inversion; and supplied a polynomial-size CLIQUE reduction whose guard, vertex, and edge weights force exactly an s-vertex lowest tied block. Exact scripts checked 210 graph/target instances through k=4, 1,536 weighted observation schedules, 120 one-missing sweeps, 145 inversion intervals, the 3/4-versus-1 constrained-support witness, and a case where equality faces raise 8/9 to 1. Current literature checks locate arbitrary-missing WMW tests and tie warnings but no supplied-design chamber optimizer or explicit-support hardness result. The cvcrand source confirms a generated support and a distinct residual-contrast test; only a new prespecified-endpoint rank option is claimed. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Machine-check the midrank subset-sum equality lemma and its lowest-tied-block consequence used by the CLIQUE converse. EARLY KILL TEST: Re-run internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/verify_exp_attrition_chamber_p1.py, requiring the equality-face result and every small CLIQUE equivalence; for any cvcrand adapter, enumerate sharp-null rejection mass and reject conditioning on survivors or the selected row. open_problems.open_problem: Does the supremum upper-tail Fisher p-value for a Wilcoxon treated-rank sum with midranks, arbitrary treatment-indexed observation masks, and a rationally weighted fixed-count assignment support admit an exact complete weak-order chamber characterization that includes equality faces?

source_refs.claim: Maximizes Fisher p-values over missing-outcome completions, but obtains closed forms from exchangeable assignment and breaks ties by unit index rather than using midranks.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peizan Sheng, Zeyang Yu

source_refs.claim: Establishes Fisher-test validity and inversion for any fully specified assignment mechanism, but does not optimize over missing completions.
source_refs.author: Xiaokang Luo, Tirthankar Dasgupta, Minge Xie, Regina Y. Liu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Argues that exact permutation tests retaining tied observations and using midranks are preferable to omitting ties or randomly breaking them.
source_refs.author: Markus Neuhäuser, Graeme D. Ruxton

source_refs.claim: Shows that holding censoring indicators fixed over reassignment can invalidate randomization inference and instead lets the observed set vary with assignment.
source_refs.author: Wen Wei Loh, Michael G. Hudgens, John D. Clemens, Mohammad Ali, Michael E. Emch

open_problems.why_unsolved: Li, Sheng, and Yu remove the missing-completion optimization from the null tail by using a distribution-free rank law under exchangeable assignments and an index-based total ordering. For an explicitly weighted, nonexchangeable support, the null tail depends on the outcome weak order itself; treatment-indexed masks additionally change which ranks enter at each supported assignment. Midranks make equality strata mathematically active, so perturbing tied completions into strict orders need not preserve the tail. Luo et al. supply arbitrary-mechanism validity but no optimizer, while the tied-rank literature computes a distribution for a fixed completed sample rather than maximizing it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite chamber theorem partitioning completion space into complete weak-order cells, including equality faces, on which all assignment-specific midrank sums and tail indicators are fixed, together with supremum attainment and unconditional finite-population validity of the resulting worst-case p-value.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from attrition-induced failure of the ordinary Fisher test to worst-case completion inference; the new work should mirror that arc while isolating the loss of exchangeability and deterministic tie-breaking.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Attrition leaves sharp-null outcomes incomplete -> the realized statistic and randomization law become unknown -> worst-case p-values restore validity -> weighted supplied designs with assignment-indexed masks and midranks require a weak-order chamber optimizer

method_exemplars.technique: Form the supremum Fisher p-value over legal completions and prove pointwise domination of the true oracle p-value before averaging under the assignment law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the exact validity skeleton needed after replacing the exchangeable closed-form extremizer with a chamber-based optimizer.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode exact tied Wilcoxon rank-sum distributions through generating-polynomial coefficient extraction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats ties as part of the exact null law and provides a checkable computation primitive once a chamber fixes the midrank vector.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove super-uniformity directly under a fully specified assignment mass function and derive coverage by inversion of the discrete p-value function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result must remain valid for arbitrary rational weights rather than an exchangeable support.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the parameterized computational-complexity frontier for maximizing the exact tied-rank tail over missing completions on an explicitly listed rational weighted support: fixed-parameter tractability in the number of missing outcomes versus NP-completeness when that number varies?

source_refs.claim: Calls the general worst-case p-value computationally intractable and obtains a closed form only after exploiting distribution-free rank statistics under exchangeable assignment.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peizan Sheng, Zeyang Yu

source_refs.claim: Gives recursive algorithms for exact significance tests under restricted sequential randomization rules, illustrating that exactness can be computationally specialized to design structure.
source_refs.author: Cyrus R. Mehta, Nitin R. Patel, L. J. Wei

source_refs.claim: Computes fixed-sample exact Wilcoxon distributions with ties by polynomial multiplication and coefficient extraction, but does not optimize over unknown completions.
source_refs.author: Andrew V. Sills
source_refs.venue: Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods

source_refs.claim: Provides the classical polynomial-reduction framework and establishes CLIQUE as an NP-complete source problem.
source_refs.author: Richard M. Karp

open_problems.why_unsolved: The exact-test literature reports combinatorial growth, recursions, dynamic programs, or Monte Carlo approximations, whereas Li, Sheng, and Yu avoid the hard optimizer through exchangeability. The scan found no complexity classification for an input that explicitly lists weighted fixed-count assignments, assignment-specific masks, tied ranks, and a tail threshold. A hardness proof cannot merely invoke exponential enumeration: it must encode a graph instance into polynomial-bit rational support weights and prove the converse, including the possibility that equality completions create extra tail mass. Conversely, a fixed-k algorithm must enumerate complete weak-order cells rather than only strict rankings.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact O((2n+1)^k n|Omega| poly(bits)) algorithm with a linear one-missing sweep, paired with an NP-completeness theorem for variable k via a polynomial-size rational weighted-support reduction from CLIQUE and an explicit membership-in-NP certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames computation as the central obstacle created by worst-case completion and gives the closest motivation arc for locating the exact tractability boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Worst-case completion preserves validity -> naive optimization is computationally intractable -> exchangeability yields a special closed form -> supplied weighted supports call for a fixed-k versus variable-k complexity classification

method_exemplars.technique: Use a polynomial many-one reduction from CLIQUE with a bidirectional witness argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested characterization must show that a high-tail completion exists exactly when the source graph contains a clique of the target size.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit finite state structure induced by a restricted assignment rule to recursively aggregate exact tail probability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest classical example of replacing brute-force exact randomization inference with an algorithm tied to explicit design structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent tied-rank tail counts by coefficients of a finite generating polynomial.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an exact tied-rank computation against which fixed-k chamber enumeration can be compared and verified.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the attrition-robust exact p-value curve for a constant additive treatment effect be inverted over all real effect values in finite quadratic time under an explicitly weighted support and a midrank tie convention?

source_refs.claim: Gives an unambiguous Fisher-test inversion procedure with guaranteed coverage for fully specified assignment mechanisms and emphasizes the discrete p-value curve.
source_refs.author: Xiaokang Luo, Tirthankar Dasgupta, Minge Xie, Regina Y. Liu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Obtains exact confidence intervals by inverting randomization tests for bounded nulls and effect quantiles, using monotonicity properties of effect-increasing rank statistics.
source_refs.author: Devin Caughey, Allan Dafoe, Xinran Li, Luke Miratrix
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Constructs finite-population-valid confidence regions with missing outcomes through imputation and re-imputation, with Monte Carlo convergence in the number of re-imputations.
source_refs.author: Siyu Heng, Jiawei Zhang, Yang Feng
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Builds valid worst-case randomization p-values for sharp and bounded treatment-effect nulls under sample attrition, but does not supply the weighted-support midrank inversion frontier.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peizan Sheng, Zeyang Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical Fisher inversion varies an additive effect through a discrete p-value function, while attrition robustness adds an inner supremum over completions. Under a weighted nonexchangeable support, the maximizing chamber can switch as the hypothesized effect crosses an observed-outcome difference, and a midrank equality face at a breakpoint can change the tail rather than being recovered from either neighboring open interval. Generic numerical inversion and monotonicity arguments for exchangeable effect-increasing statistics therefore do not identify every endpoint or its open or closed status.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of the finite effect-breakpoint set and equality-face values yielding an exact O(n^2) sweep that returns the complete confidence set, including endpoint inclusion rules, with finite-population coverage inherited from worst-case p-value validity.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation treats the entire discrete Fisher p-value curve as the inferential object and motivates exact inversion rather than grid search.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A Fisher test gives a discrete p-value at each sharp effect -> inversion should produce a coverage-guaranteed confidence set -> grid inversion can miss discontinuities -> attrition and equality faces require a finite exact breakpoint sweep

method_exemplars.technique: Invert the complete discrete Fisher p-value function and prove coverage directly from test validity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target resolution is an exact confidence set under a known, potentially nonuniform assignment mass function.

method_exemplars.technique: Use effect-increasing rank statistics to establish p-value monotonicity and interval structure under bounded-null inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest rank-based inversion argument; the missing step is handling a completion supremum whose optimizer and equality behavior change with the effect.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace an unidentified oracle p-value with its supremum over all missing-outcome completions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each effect-specific test in the desired inversion must use this attrition-robust envelope before the breakpoint sweep can begin.

open_problems.open_problem: For a prespecified cluster-level endpoint in a covariate-constrained trial, can a new Wilcoxon-midrank option obtain exact attrition-robust conditional inference by reusing the saved randomization support without conditioning on survivors or the selected assignment row?

source_refs.claim: The cvcrand workflow saves the constrained randomization space and cptest permutes only within it, but cptest uses cluster residual-mean contrasts rather than a rank statistic.
source_refs.author: Hengshi Yu, Fan Li, John A. Gallis, Elizabeth L. Turner

source_refs.claim: Proves correct significance levels for a randomization test conditional on a prespecified covariate-balance partition.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Hennessy, Tirthankar Dasgupta, Luke Miratrix, Cassandra Pattanayak, Pradipta Sarkar

source_refs.claim: Shows that deleting attrited units can distort size and proposes worst-case randomization p-values, but its tractable rank procedures target exchangeable individual-level assignments.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peizan Sheng, Zeyang Yu

source_refs.claim: Demonstrates that fixing the observed or censored subset across reassignments can fail to control size when observation status is treatment-dependent.
source_refs.author: Wen Wei Loh, Michael G. Hudgens, John D. Clemens, Mohammad Ali, Michael E. Emch

open_problems.why_unsolved: The saved cvcrand space is a legitimate prespecified conditional assignment support, but the documented cptest statistic is a residualized cluster-mean contrast and its guarantees do not automatically transfer to a Wilcoxon rank sum with attrition. Conditioning after treatment on surviving clusters, or retaining only assignments compatible with the selected realized row, changes the assignment law in an outcome-dependent manner. A valid rank option must evaluate every saved assignment with its treatment-indexed mask and maximize over missing endpoint completions while leaving the saved support and its probabilities unchanged.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A conditional finite-population validity corollary and executable reference algorithm for a prespecified cluster endpoint that applies the weighted-support chamber p-value to exactly the saved constrained support, plus a sharp counterexample showing why survivor-conditioned or selected-row-conditioned supports are invalid.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents the design-to-analysis workflow, saved constrained space, and current cptest interface that a prospective rank option would extend.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Few clusters make baseline imbalance likely -> covariate constraints create a prespecified acceptable support -> valid analysis must reuse that saved support -> an attrition-robust rank endpoint needs a new support-preserving option rather than unchanged cptest

method_exemplars.technique: Prove conditional randomization validity by fixing an ex ante partition cell and averaging only under its induced assignment law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It licenses use of a prespecified saved support while showing why post-outcome survivor conditioning is a different operation.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry the enumerated constrained randomization matrix from design into analysis and compute the reference distribution only over that matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed rank procedure should plug into the same saved-support workflow while changing the statistic and missingness handling.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a conservative exact p-value by taking the worst case over missing endpoint values instead of deleting attrited units.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the inference move needed inside each saved cluster assignment after adapting the optimizer to the nonexchangeable constrained support.

literature_map:
Fisher (1935), The Design of Experiments, is the foundational sharp-null design-based anchor: inference follows the assignment mechanism.
Wilcoxon (1945), Biometrics Bulletin, supplies the treated rank-sum statistic, with average ranks as the classical treatment of ties.
Mehta, Patel, and Wei (1988, Biometrika) compute exact tests under restricted sequential randomization rules, showing design-specific recursions can replace naive enumeration.
Hennessy et al. (2016, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:1510.06817) prove validity when conditioning on an ex ante covariate-balance partition.
Yu, Li, Gallis, and Turner (2019, The R Journal) require cvcrand analyses to reuse the saved constrained support; cptest uses residualized cluster-mean contrasts, not Wilcoxon ranks.
Loh et al. (2020, Biometrics, arXiv:1803.02302) show that holding censoring status fixed over reassignments can invalidate randomization inference and leave exact theoretical size control as a gap.
Luo et al. (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:2004.08472) cover any fully specified assignment mechanism and give guaranteed Fisher-test inversion, but do not optimize over missing completions.
Caughey et al. (2023, JRSSB, arXiv:2101.09195) develop bounded-null and effect-quantile inversion using effect-increasing rank statistics; distribution-free rank arguments rely on exchangeability and specified tie rules.
Heussen et al. (2024, Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research) preserve randomization distributions through missing-data imputations under randomization-based missingness conditions.
Neuhäuser and Ruxton (2024, PLOS ONE) argue that exact permutation WMW tests should retain ties and use midranks rather than omit or randomly break tied observations.
Sills (2024, Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, arXiv:2409.05741) derives exact tied Wilcoxon null distributions by generating-polynomial coefficient extraction, but for fixed completed data.
Heng, Zhang, and Feng (2026 print/2025 online, JASA, arXiv:2310.18556) give finite-population-exact imputation and re-imputation tests and valid confidence regions under nearly minimal assignment-invariant missingness conditions.
Li, Sheng, and Yu (2025, arXiv:2507.00795) are the nearest anchor: they maximize Fisher p-values over attrition completions and obtain closed forms under exchangeable assignments, but use deterministic index tie-breaking.
Across these strands, the unoccupied intersection is exact optimization over arbitrary treatment-indexed masks on an explicitly weighted fixed-count support with midrank equality faces; the search also found no published fixed-parameter or NP-completeness classification for that optimizer.
